correctness.rationale: Verified head-to-tail. Baseline s_B^2=L/pi with L=ln(2048(1+2^128)) matches Micciancio-Regev Lemma 3.3 form for lambda1=1, eps=2^-128. Z^1024 is R=Z[x]/(x^1024+1) under coefficient embedding, self-dual, hence a valid dual of a power-of-two cyclotomic ideal lattice. First-shell lower bound tail>=2048*exp(-pi s'^2) with s'=0.85 s_B gives pi s'^2=(289/400)L exactly. Interval certificate (289/400)L_HI<=101*ln2_LO checked with certified ln2 enclosures yields tail>=2^11*2^-101=2^-90, 38 bits above 2^-128. Replay of output/artifacts/verify_counterexample.py prints VERIFY_OK. Embedding-scale objection fails: coefficient member has lambda1=1 so dimension-only and per-lattice baselines coincide; canonical scaling would only strengthen violation. Compared with topic.audit_preflight cheap checks, no normalization-shift, vacuity, or tiny-instance defect; no ADMISSION_DEFECT.

originality.rationale: TARGET route: admitted target was novel and both resolutions were pre-qualified as original. Fused live search over literal, equivalent (theta/smoothing/Z^n tightness), and broader (Banaszczyk/MR generic, cyclic-lattice bounds, databases) directions returns only generic upper-bound literature (Guo et al. 2025 PLOS, Peikert smoothing problem, Zheng et al. cyclic/ideal bounds, Espitau et al.) with no uniform 15% cyclotomic claim at N=1024 eps=2^-128 and no recorded tail>=2^-90 lower bound for Z^1024 at 0.85 width. Prior upper bounds cannot imply a lower-bound refutation; no broader census or table exhaustively covers it. The two-line first-shell derivation is the proof itself, not a prior recorded result, and no prior source states the exact 38-bit violation. Hence the negative resolution is new.

value.rationale: Complete negative TARGET resolution with sharpness value beyond mere falsity. It exhibits an explicit extremal family member (unit-ideal dual Z^1024) violating the claimed uniform 15% improvement by 38 bits (factor >=2^38) and in fact proves no constant factor c<1 can work uniformly (needs c^2>=139 ln2/L=1-O(2^-128)). This maps the true optimal-constant boundary, blocks wasted tightening attempts, and tightens understanding of every downstream dual-Fourier / worst-case-to-average-case analysis that pays smoothing cost. N=1024 and 2^-128 are standard cryptographic targets, motivated before computation, not an arbitrary slice; first-shell simplicity does not make it a cheap type/normalization/vacuity defect. Matches admitted negative-resolution value case; no ADMISSION_DEFECT.
